title: From complaint to notice to another permit
question: Once a building is cited, what does it take to clear the notice, and how many notices are caused by paperwork running out?
finding: Building Inspection issued a first notice of violation on 47,664 complaints since 2015. Clearing one took a median 77 days, and 8% of notices from 2015 to 2023 are still open. 561 notices cite an expired or cancelled permit and 6,103 cite work without a permit. 10,067 building permits were filed to answer a notice or complaint; 103 of those are also permits to finish or renew an earlier permit. 4,587 lots drew notices on three or more separate complaints.
how: Complaints with a first-notice date since 2015, joined to the notice items that tick 'expired permit', 'cancelled permit' or 'work without permit'. Days to clear run from the first notice to the abated or closed date. Permits to answer a notice are building permits whose stated purpose says to comply with a notice or complaint.
limits: Most notices are about real hazards, and citing unpermitted work is the department doing its job. A notice staying open can mean an owner who will not act. What the data adds is the loop: a permit that lapses becomes a violation, and the cure is another permit. The Controller found in 2021 that the fines 'may not be sufficient to deter misconduct' on large projects; the fee and penalty amounts are in the fee schedule, not in this data.
